title: Never Have I Ever: Life & Uni

items.text: Never have I ever skipped a lecture to sleep in.
Never have I ever handed in an assignment one minute before the deadline.
Never have I ever started an essay the night before it was due.
Never have I ever pretended to have read the book.
Never have I ever eaten instant noodles three days in a row.
Never have I ever lied about my age.
Never have I ever invented an excuse to leave a party early.
Never have I ever googled myself.
Never have I ever cried in a library.
Never have I ever called a teacher "mum" or "dad".
Never have I ever blamed a smell on someone else.
Never have I ever regifted a present.
Never have I ever muted the family group chat forever.
Never have I ever read someone's messages over their shoulder.
Never have I ever eaten a flatmate's food from the shared fridge.
Never have I ever pretended to be ill to skip work or school.
Never have I ever sent a voice note longer than five minutes.
Never have I ever fallen asleep during a lecture.
Never have I ever cheated at a board game.
Never have I ever exaggerated on my CV.
Never have I ever borrowed clothes and never given them back.
Never have I ever had a crush on a teacher.
Never have I ever cut my own hair.
Never have I ever watched a whole season in one day.
Never have I ever texted "on my way" while still in bed.
Never have I ever laughed so hard I snorted.
Never have I ever pretended to work while doing nothing.
Never have I ever spent a whole paycheck in one weekend.
Never have I ever sung karaoke sober.
Never have I ever turned up to a party I wasn't invited to.
Never have I ever taken the last slice without asking.
Never have I ever eavesdropped on strangers on a train.
Never have I ever read the last page of a book first.
Never have I ever eaten cereal for dinner.
Never have I ever forgotten someone's name right after hearing it.
Never have I ever missed the last train home.
Never have I ever stayed in pyjamas for an entire weekend.
Never have I ever argued with a stranger in the comments.
Never have I ever pretended not to be home when the doorbell rang.
Never have I ever told my parents an exam went better than it did.
Never have I ever slept in a train station.
